_comment: The committed anti-convergence clause of the hypothesis-authoring agent.
app_spec.xml, Hypothesis Authoring Agent, feature 210:
'Agent applies an explicit anti-convergence clause, so a tree never
collapses into 400 parameter tweaks of one indicator.'
docs/alpha-engine-prd.md C3 is where the clause comes from: the discovery
agent's prompt adapts the paper's Listing 1 'nearly verbatim, keeping in
particular ... the explicit anti-convergence clause.  Without it, a
discovery tree collapses into 400 parameter tweaks of one indicator.'
docs/nullius-tech-architecture.md 14.1 says why it is not optional: 'A
bad proposal is caught by the evaluator at a cost of one trial charge.  A
converged tree is not caught by anything.  At roots, a weak model's
failure mode is proposing the 400th variant of one indicator - every node
scores plausibly, the budget is fully consumed, and nothing in the
pipeline detects it.'
The clause below is the text the agent is asked to write under.  It is
the ONE place in this member where prose is the deliverable, and it stays
on the right side of the line PRD C3 and 14.1 draw: it forbids a shape of
proposal without naming a direction to search in.  It carries no finding
distilled from campaign history - no 'this theme has been paying off', no
summary of what has been tried - which is the injection feature 208 makes
a refusal of.  A negative constraint cannot over-constrain a search; a
prose prior about where to look can.
The compile in packages/signal-agent/src/signal_agent/_anti_convergence.py
refuses this file and any change to it that is not a marker plus one
clause with a slug, a title and a non-empty text - so the clause is not a
convention the next edit can forget.  A campaign's prompt must carry this
text: the gate's carries()/require_in() screen a prompt against the
committed clause, and a prompt that does not carry it is refused by name
rather than shipped with the clause silently missing.  That is the
'applies' half of the feature's sentence, and its dual is feature 208,
which refuses what must NOT be in the prompt.
The applied half - 'so a tree never collapses into 400 parameter tweaks
of one indicator' - is not configuration: the gate compares a proposal's
structure against the structures the tree already holds, with every
numeric literal erased, and refuses a proposal that differs from a node
the campaign holds in its parameters alone.  That rule is code rather
than a field here, because what counts as 'the same indicator' is a
property of the tree this member walks and not a number an edit could
tune.
Nothing here is a scored input, and nothing here is a threshold: the
clause refuses a *shape* of proposal and never prices one.  'A converged
tree' is not the number of nodes, it is the number of distinct mechanisms
a tree holds - which is feature 215's figure, measured over the tree, not
this law's.

clause.title: The explicit anti-convergence clause
clause.text: Before proposing, read the complete history in full. Do not propose another variant of a mechanism this tree already holds: if a proposal differs from an existing node only in its parameters - a lookback, a window, a threshold, a multiplier, a scaling constant - it is the same hypothesis re-submitted, and it is refused. Every root must open a mechanism the tree does not already contain, or make a structural change to one it does, and the proposal must state which. The failure this clause exists to prevent is a discovery tree that collapses into 400 parameter tweaks of one indicator: every node scores plausibly, the budget is fully consumed, and nothing in the pipeline detects it. A converged tree is not caught by anything else.
